newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower, with local traders echoing the prolonged absence of buyers in the market.

Checks with several trading houses showed no business was concluded on Thursday. Local traders also dismissed claims by a Singapore agent that Malaysian exporters sold about 400-500 tonnes of SMR20 at about 287-288 Malaysian cents a kg.
"That's absurd to say the least," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur. "The market's just dead."
The MRELB quoted April RSS1 buyer was quoted at 302 cents ($1.23) a kg, down one cent from Wednesday.
April SMR20 buyer ended 1.50 cents down at 288 cents.
Traders offered the SMR20 at 292 cents a kg, SMR CV at 354, SMR L at 333, SMR 5 at 298, SMR 10 at 288 and latex at 235.
They said producers were trying hard to match the low prices in Indonesia but were hampered by the high costs in Malaysia.
The INRO five-day average was at 231.74 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 19 from 232.13 Mar 18. The daily indicator was at 230.41 from 231.77 previously.
